# Implementation Plan: Normalize Application Typography

**Branch**: `082-normalize-app-typography` | **Date**: 2026-08-20 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/Users/stevenyi/work/blue-electron/specs/082-normalize-app-typography/spec.md`

**Note**: This file is generated by the Spec Kit planning workflow. Task generation is captured separately in `tasks.md`.

## Summary

Replace Blue's overlapping 8–18 px legacy, Tailwind-default, arbitrary, CSS,
SVG, and canvas text sizes with one macOS-HIG-guided semantic catalog. Define
exactly seven `text-role-*` Tailwind utilities and matching `--text-role-*` CSS
variables in the renderer's CSS-first Tailwind theme, set Body as the inherited
13/16 baseline, and adapt dense geometry instead of shrinking application text
below 11 logical pixels. Preserve project-authored Blue Synth Builder font data
unchanged, enforce the boundary through a cross-platform CI-blocking static
inventory, and verify rendered metrics, contrast, density, zoom, and geometry
with a deterministic macOS visual matrix. Make `docs/typography.md` the durable
design authority and direct all UI work to it from `AGENTS.md`.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.8.x in strict mode; React 19.2.x; CSS processed by Tailwind CSS 4.1.x; Node.js ECMAScript modules for repository audits

**Primary Dependencies**: Electron 35.7.5/Chromium renderer, Tailwind CSS CSS-first `@theme` configuration, Vite 7.3.x, Dockview 5.2.x, CodeMirror 6, inline SVG and Canvas 2D surfaces, existing Roboto and monospaced font packages

**Storage**: N/A. Typography is presentation metadata; `.blue` XML, project-authored font values, program settings, and application zoom persistence remain unchanged

**Testing**: Vitest 4.1.x renderer/unit tests, Node's built-in test runner for the static audit, Tailwind/Vite renderer build, existing BSB project round-trip tests, cross-platform root `pnpm test`, macOS manual visual acceptance at high and standard/equivalent density, workspace lint, and `git diff --check`

**Target Platform**: Electron desktop application on macOS, Windows, and Linux; macOS is the primary visual reference and acceptance platform

**Project Type**: Desktop application renderer normalization plus repository validation and design documentation

**Performance Goals**: No measurable runtime interaction or rendering regression; typography lookup remains native CSS inheritance/variables, and the source audit remains suitable for every pull-request test run

**Constraints**: Exactly seven semantic roles and six metric pairs; 11 logical-pixel application-text floor at 100% zoom; 50%–300% existing app zoom retained; exact role line heights; Body fallback in every renderer entry point; no default Tailwind size scale, retired token, arbitrary application font size, duplicate token source, project-data coercion, new font family, IPC, settings, or persistence change

**Scale/Scope**: Approximately 187 production renderer files with typography assignments; 626 legacy utility occurrences, 57 legacy variable references, 288 Tailwind-default utility occurrences, 26 arbitrary size utilities, direct CSS/SVG/canvas assignments, all application-owned windows and dense editor surfaces, seven roles, and two display-density acceptance profiles

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

- **Portable data core**: PASS. All production changes remain in `@blue/app` renderer presentation code or repository scripts/docs. `@blue/data` receives no UI, DOM, Electron, Node, or dynamic-import dependency.
- **Java and project compatibility**: PASS. Java Blue was consulted as historical density evidence, but Blue intentionally adopts an 11 px application-owned floor where Java commonly used 10 pt. `.blue` XML and imported/user-authored BSB font values remain exact canonical project data and are covered by focused round-trip validation.
- **Canonical ownership and contracts**: PASS. The main-process `BlueData` document remains the sole owner of project-authored font values and existing program settings remain the owner of zoom. The CSS theme owns application typography metrics; `docs/typography.md` owns human design guidance; the audit owns no runtime state. No IPC, preload, migration, or recovery contract is added.
- **Runtime and engine isolation**: PASS/N/A. Java lifecycle, filesystem/process access, ZeroMQ, engine-client protocols, and generated artifacts are untouched; renderers gain presentation-only CSS assignments.
- **Host-path portability**: PASS. The audit uses Node `path` helpers, emits repository-relative forward-slash identifiers only at its report boundary, and runs through the existing macOS/Windows/Linux root test matrix. No host filesystem value is persisted or compared with embedded text.
- **Verification evidence**: PASS. The design requires scanner fixture tests for every syntax category, exact token/body-baseline assertions, focused geometry and class-string regressions, BSB authored-font round trips, renderer build, root tests/lint, a deterministic macOS visual/contrast/zoom matrix at two densities, and `git diff --check`.

**Structure Decision**: Keep the runtime change entirely inside the existing
`@blue/app` renderer and keep `styles/index.css` as the single machine source of
role metrics. Tailwind utilities, custom CSS, Dockview, CodeMirror, inline SVG,
and drawn text all consume the same emitted variables; a renderer-only helper may
resolve CSS variables before composing Canvas `font` strings. Add a separate
typography audit because its semantic-role, line-height, SVG/canvas, and authored
project exception rules differ from the existing color-theme audit. Put exception
records in a machine-readable block in the canonical guide so human policy and CI
enforcement cannot drift. No Tailwind JavaScript configuration, preload, IPC,
main-process, settings, project-model, Java-runtime, or engine change is needed.

## Phase 0: Research

Research is captured in [research.md](research.md). Key decisions:

- Map Apple's macOS built-in text-style point metrics one-to-one to unzoomed
  Electron CSS logical pixels; do not apply a physical 4/3 point-to-pixel
  conversion.
- Use seven role-prefixed utilities/variables: Large Title, Title 2, Title 3,
  Headline, Body, Callout, and Subheadline. The prefix prevents reuse of the
  ambiguous retired `--text-body` vocabulary.
- Reset Tailwind's complete `--text-*` namespace in `@theme static`, define only
  the seven approved role pairs, use exact px values, and establish Body on the
  renderer root rather than changing the HTML rem baseline.
- Keep weight and font family orthogonal to size roles; Headline is paired with
  bold at its call sites, while existing Roboto/monospace choices remain.
- Use direct CSS variables for CSS/SVG and resolve the same variables before
  composing Canvas font strings; do not introduce a second TypeScript catalog.
- Preserve project-authored BSB values through exact, occurrence-counted
  exceptions and round-trip tests. Nearby BSB application chrome is not exempt.
- Add a dedicated source audit whose complete inventory and exact allowlist are
  CI-blocking through root tests/lint; namespace reset alone cannot block
  Tailwind arbitrary values.
- Use manual rendered acceptance because the feature spans native menus, many
  windows, data-dependent canvases, contrast states, and density-dependent
  geometry that static analysis cannot prove.

## Implementation Strategy

1. Add the canonical guide, scanner fixture tests, semantic role definitions, and
   Body inheritance. Keep the legacy/default tokens available only as a temporary
   local migration bridge so untouched surfaces do not lose styling mid-change.
2. Build the complete production typography inventory, classify each occurrence
   by semantic purpose, and register only exact authored/non-text exceptions.
3. Migrate ordinary application controls first, then direct CSS/Dockview and
   CodeMirror consumers, and finally geometry-sensitive SVG/canvas editors.
4. Preserve authored BSB bindings while normalizing adjacent application chrome;
   run round-trip and focused geometry tests as each boundary changes.
5. Remove the migration bridge, apply the complete namespace reset, make the exact
   token/production audit pass, wire it into root tests/lint, execute the
   two-density macOS visual matrix and zoom matrix, and update recorded evidence
   before the repository-wide validation handoff.

## Post-Design Constitution Check

- **Portable data core**: PASS. The contracts keep CSS/token resolution in the renderer and repository scanning in `scripts/`; no `@blue/data` production change is designed.
- **Java and project compatibility**: PASS. The data model and system contract explicitly separate application assignments from project-authored BSB font values, name the intentional 11 px divergence from Java density, and require exact round-trip fixtures.
- **Canonical ownership and contracts**: PASS. `index.css` is the one metric source, `docs/typography.md` is the one human design/exception authority, `BlueData` remains project owner, and every scanner or visual result is disposable evidence rather than application state.
- **Runtime and engine isolation**: PASS/N/A. The contracts add no runtime host capability and touch no engine or Java execution boundary.
- **Host-path portability**: PASS. The audit contract normalizes report paths only at the output boundary, forbids broad directory exemptions, and requires identical cross-platform results through root CI.
- **Verification evidence**: PASS. The audit and visual contracts define deterministic pass/fail conditions, the quickstart names focused and repository-wide commands, and no required acceptance claim is left without automated or recorded manual evidence.
